COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPSS No.1597 of 2021
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Ms. Monika Pant, Advocate, for the 
petitioner.
Mr. Rakesh Kunwar, Additional CSC, for 
the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Rajesh Sharma, Advocate, for the 
respondent. 
The petitioner in the present writ petition 
has put a challenge to the impugned order dated 
18.12.2020, which was passed by the respondent 
No.2, whereby the benefits of the 3rd ACP, which 
was granted to the petitioner, was later withdrawn.
Initially, when the writ petition was taken 
up, on account of certain typographical error, the 
petitioner sought a liberty to file an amendment 
application to make the necessary rectification in 
the pleadings made in the writ petition.
The said permission was granted by an order 
dated 06.12.2021.
Accordingly, the amendment application i.e.
(IA No.02 of 2021) has been filed by the petitioner.
After having gone through the contents of the 
amendment application, since the nature of the 
amendment is only by way of a correction of the 
typographical error, which has chanced in the writ 
petition, the same would stand allowed, and the 
necessary amendment as prayed for by adding 
paragraphs provided in paragraph Nos.5 and 6, of 
the amendment application i.e. permitted to be 
carried out by the petitioner in the memo of writ 
petition. The petitioner would undertake the 
exercise of supplying the amended memo of writ 
petition within a period of two weeks from today.
Therefore, three weeks’ time is granted to 
the respondents to file counter affidavit.
List thereafter. 
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 24.12.2021

In
WPSS No. 1597 of 2021
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
(through V.C.)
1. Mrs. Monika Pant, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, learned Standing Counsel for 
the State.
3. Mr. Rajesh Sharma, learned counsel for respondent 
nos. 2 and 3.
4. The ACP benefits including the salary for the 
period of suspension has been withheld by the 
respondent department on the ground that the petitioner 
is facing a criminal prosecution though with the same set 
of charges the departmental proceeding was initiated in 
which the petitioner has been exonerated. Now, the 
question is even in the departmental proceeding the 
petitioner has been exonerated from all the charges how 
the respondents can withheld the benefits of the ACP 
including the arrears of salary for the suspension period.
5. Put up this matter on 17.09.2025.
6. On that day learned counsel Mr. Rajesh Sharma 
will explain on this.
7. Urgency application stands disposed of.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPSS No. 1597 of 2021
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mrs. Monika Pant, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. I.P. Kohli, learned Standing Counsel assisted 
by Mr. Tarun Mohan, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. Mr. Rajesh Sharma, learned counsel for respondent 
nos. 2 and 3.
4. Apparently the respondent illegally withhold the 
gratuity and the consequential benefits like third ACP 
and the leave encashment of the petitioner pursuant to 
the order impugned dated 28.12.2024. Apparently by the 
order impugned all the benefits have been withheld on 
the ground that the same be subject to the final outcome 
of Criminal Appeal No. 262 of 2019. The petitioner was 
placed under suspension but the disciplinary proceeding 
was never been initiated against him and by that time on 
31.12.2020 the petitioner retired from service. 
Surprisingly, just before two days of the retirement on 
28.12.2020 the Regional Manager passed order impugned, 
whereby, the petitioner was reinstated subject to this 
condition that the other benefits will be subject to the 
decision of the criminal appeal, which has been preferred 
by the petitioner against his conviction. Impugned order 
on the face of it appears to be illegal and dehors the rules,
since at no point of time the disciplinary proceeding was 
initiated against the petitioner.
5. Put up this matter on 26.11.2025.
6. On that day the Managing Director either to appear 
in person or to show cause why and under which 
provision of law the benefits have been withheld 
pursuant to the order impugned.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 21.11.2025

3. Mr. Rajesh Sharma, learned counsel for respondent 
nos. 2 and 3.
4. Mr. Rajesh Sharma, learned counsel for the 
Corporation, apprise to this court that the order 
impugned dated 18.12.2020 has been recalled by an order 
dated 24.11.2025 passed by the Regional Manager and the 
decision has been taken to pay all post-retiral benefits 
towards the ACP, leave encashment and gratuity as well 
as the salary for the period of suspension. He also 
submits that within two weeks all the benefits as above 
shall be released.
